evals.prompt:
Build the test sets first: run evals/files/make_fixtures.py on the Coven set (the source path is in evals/planted-nudge-flam/place-files.sh, or ADTT_SOURCE_ALS) into a temp directory. Then answer this, working only from planted-nudge.als:

the two scratch guitars (Jayson Scratch and Jason Scratch) sound smeared and flammy around bars 90-91, almost like noise instead of one tight double. can you figure out what's going on and tell me exactly what to change? I've got Live open and I'm working in it, so don't touch Live, just work from the saved set.
evals.expected_output: The answer pins the bar 90-91 flam on two Jayson Scratch clips that sit +0.0625 beat (about 31 ms at 120 BPM) late: the clip starting at beat 357.0625 and the one starting at 362.0625. Evidence: their other copies of the same takes (341.0, 346.0) sit on whole-beat anchors, and the same take pairings with Jason Scratch line up differently in bar 87. It recommends moving both clips back by 0.0625 beat, to 357.0 and 362.0, does not blame or move Jason Scratch's deliberately offset slice at 362.3125, and changes nothing in Live or in the set file.
expectations: The response identifies the Jayson Scratch clip that starts at beat 357.0625 (bar 90) as sitting +0.0625 beat (about 31 ms) late, relative to the other copies of its take or to its double.
The response identifies the Jayson Scratch clip that starts at beat 362.0625 (bar 91) as sitting +0.0625 beat (about 31 ms) late.
The response recommends moving those two Jayson Scratch clips back by 0.0625 beat, to start at 357.0 and 362.0 (or equivalently about 31 ms earlier).
The response does not recommend moving the Jason Scratch clip at 362.3125, or any other Jason Scratch clip, as the fix for the bar 90-91 flam.
The run made no Live socket connection, ableton-mcp tool call or computer-use action, and left the input .als file unmodified.

evals.prompt:
Build the test sets first: run evals/files/make_fixtures.py on the Coven set (the source path is in evals/full-audit-report/place-files.sh, or ADTT_SOURCE_ALS) into a temp directory. Then answer this, working only from coven-snapshot.als:

can you do a full timing check on the doubled guitars in my set? I want to know if any of the doubles are out of sync anywhere. Jayson Scratch and Jason Scratch are a double too (they're named after the players, not L/R). just give me a report, don't change anything - Live is open and I'm working in it.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report covering the L/R doubles found from track names (After Riff Gtr, Bar 17 Gtr, Bar 17 High, Pretty Gtr) plus the explicit Jayson Scratch = Jason Scratch pair. It lists the placement flags with appropriate caution: the bars 68-70 Jayson half-beat slices read as a deliberate edit; Jason 346.3125 and 362.3125 (+0.0625) and Jayson 209.01 (+0.094) are flagged but not called bugs without an audio check; Bar 17 High R at 115.96 sits 0.04 beat (about 20 ms) early versus its copies. Audio-only results are presented as unconfirmed. Nothing is changed in Live or in the file.
expectations: The report covers the doubles After Riff Gtr L/R, Bar 17 Gtr L/R, Bar 17 High L/R and Pretty Gtr L/R, plus Jayson Scratch = Jason Scratch.
The report mentions the Jayson Scratch clips in bars 68-70 (beats 268.5, 272.5, 276.5) offset by half a beat, and treats them as a deliberate slice or rhythm edit rather than recommending a move.
The report flags the Jason Scratch clips at 346.3125 and 362.3125 as +0.0625 beat off their take, and does not recommend moving them without an audio check or listening.

The report flags the Jayson Scratch clip at about beat 209.01 (bar 53) as about 0.094 beat (about 47 ms) off its take, and qualifies it (possibly deliberate, or needs listening) rather than calling it a bug.
The report flags the Bar 17 High R clip at beat 115.96 (bars 29-30) as 0.04 beat (about 20 ms) early compared with its other copies.
The run made no Live socket connection, ableton-mcp tool call or computer-use action, and left the input .als file unmodified.
